steps.text: Heat a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir sausage in the hot skillet until crumbly and browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to remove sausage to a paper towel-lined plate to drain; set aside.

Pour off most of the grease from the skillet, leaving 2 to 3 tablespoons. Stir flour into grease in the skillet over medium-low heat. Whisk vigorously until roux forms, scraping the bottom of the skillet. Reduce heat to low and let roux cook for at least 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Grandma always "burned" hers a little on purpose.

Stream milk into roux, whisking constantly. After adding about 2 1/2 cups, increase heat to medium and continue cooking, whisking constantly. Bring gravy to a boil and cook to desired thickness. Add some of the sausage to gravy if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This sausage gravy uses 3 ingredients to make a thick, flavorful sauce just like Grandma used to make and serve with hot, freshly baked biscuits.

review.reviewBody: Very simple to make. The first night I thought it was a little bland so I would have only rated it with three stars. Luckily I had the left overs for lunch the next day. What a differnce that made! The sausage flavor had time to really blend with the gravy to make a wonderful meal. Next time I will simmer the gravy longer before serving to give it the extra flavor it really needs.

My mom taught me basically the same recipe. 3tbsp flour to 3 cups milk. Makes a skillet that has plenty of gravy for a family for 4-6, that are extra gravy on top people sausage usually renders the perfect amount of fat in the skillet for this recipe also. Bacon usually renders too much, so some will need to be scooped out (no problem). Both greases give good flavor to the gravy. When I measure out my flour I add about 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/8 tsp garlic powder & 1/8 tsp onion powder. All those spices are to your families preference. Leaving out or increasing to taste. A good "all season" mix such as Tex-joy is good (but I'm a control freak so I add my own). Remember, you can also salt & pepper on your plate. And I taste as in cooking and adjust seasoning.

Don't need to try! Been making it about the same for 40 years. I now add part like maybe 1/4 water then 3/4 milk. I cover the meat and just a little higher with the liquid. I use 2 heaping tablespoons flour per lb of sausage. I always add all the meat in to the gravy. This is sooooo good! Today I add some red pepper flakes to it. My mother in law told me if you like it dark in color to just add a 1/4 teaspoon of instant coffee. That does work but I never cared if it was dark or not. Its fabulous just on toast. Been great for 40 years and many many people beg me to bring it to camp. Its a hit.
I didnt get much grease from the sausage so I added butter. It took a long time for the milk to boil. I added cracked black pepper.
We love this and it is a breakfast item I make regularly! I use Jimmy Dean Hot breakfast sausage and I increased the flour to 1/4 cups. I also add minced garlic while it is cooking. Yum!

I tasted this while cooking and thought it needed at least a little extra seasoning...I added freshly ground black pepper and some dried crumbled sage. Skipped a step to make this even easier and just drained the grease off the sausage, leaving about 1 tblsp in the skillet. Then sprinkled a good heaping tblsp of flour over the meat and combined well, cooking for a minute or so. Then added the milk (didn't measure, just kept adding until the thickness was right.) Served this over thick slices of buttered french bread that I toasted under the broiler.
I use 1 lb of sage Jimmy Dean sausage and 1 lb of maple sausage. I am not a big sausage lover. but this combo worked for me.
This is my go to recipe for sausage gravy! However, I use 4 cups of whole milk to stretch the recipe, and add in 1/4 pure maple syrup. Also, a couple sprinkles of pepper!
You do not need to drain and remove the sausage. Just leave the sausage and all the grease in the pan, add more flour, enough that it soaks up most of the grease, then add the milk.

We all loved it!! I added 2 more TB of flour, used all 3 cups of milk at once, and added a few shakes of seasoned salt. I let it simmer a while until it was as thick as I liked it and flavorful. Simple and delicious!! :)

This is a good basic gravy. I didn't have sausage available so I used bacon as a substitute and added black pepper, cayenne pepper, paprika, and garlic powder to bring out more flavor. If you're cooking with bacon or prepackaged sausage I would skip adding salt.
Good base. Added 1 tsp of salt and black pepper. Also added about 1 tbsp of flour for additional thickening.
Oldie but goodie. Best way to make sausage gravy - hands down!
No changes, husband says it’s the best he has ever had!!
This quick and easy to make with ingredients that are usually right at hand. I added some cracked black pepper and salted to taste. Thank you for the recipe!
This was easy and delicious. I added salt and pepper, and a few sprinkles of hot pepper flakes, and served it over biscuits and l leftover breaded eggplant.
